newsitem.title: INDIA: India fixes state support price for summer crops.
newsitem.headline: India fixes state support price for summer crops.

text.p: The Indian government on Thursday fixed a minimum support price of 415 rupees per quintal for the 1996/97 (February-March) wheat crop, up from 380 rupees last year.
The new crop would be marketed in the 1997/98 season.
The cabinet committee on economic affairs approved the price of rapeseed/mustard to be marketed in 1997/98 at 890 rupees per quintal compared to 860 rupees in the previous season.
For safflower it fixed a price of 830 rupees per quintal for the 1997/98 marketing season, up from 800 rupees in the previous season.
The minimum support price for gram will be 740 rupees per quintal for 1997/98 compared to 700 rupees last season.
